claims.text: The dynamic mechanical behavior of HEAs stems from an interplay between pronounced local lattice distortions and dynamic recovery mechanisms.
Local lattice distortions create a spatially heterogeneous dislocation glide-resistance landscape.
Dynamic recovery mechanisms activate during high-strain-rate loading.
Temporary retardation of dislocation motion by local lattice distortions increases yield strength.
Rapid dislocation rearrangement through dynamic recovery enhances ductility and mitigates premature failure.
The competition between lattice-distortion strengthening and dynamic recovery produces a strain-rate-dependent strength-ductility synergy.
Equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni can form a homogeneous single-phase FCC HEA with significant local lattice distortion.
High mean-square atomic displacement is an appropriate quantitative indicator of significant local lattice distortion.
A strain-rate range from approximately 10^-4 to 10^2 s^-1 captures the onset of dynamic recovery without overwhelming thermal effects.
Transient adiabatic heating and high defect mobility under dynamic loading promote dislocation reconfiguration and dynamic recovery.
Dynamic loading will produce a higher yield strength than quasi-static loading of the same HEA.
Dynamic loading will maintain or enhance ductility relative to quasi-static loading of the same HEA.
The HEA will exhibit nonlinear strain-rate sensitivity with an intermediate dynamic strain rate that maximizes the proposed strength-ductility synergy.

The proposed mechanism applies to equiatomic FCC HEAs with significant local lattice distortion from room temperature to approximately 373 K, provided cryogenic inertial effects and extreme thermal softening do not dominate.
Similar dynamic behavior in a structurally similar low-MSAD control alloy would falsify the attribution of the behavior to local lattice distortion.

contradictions.description: The prediction permits ductility merely to be maintained under dynamic loading, whereas the falsification rule can reject the hypothesis when ductility is not improved. Thus, an observation of higher yield strength with unchanged ductility is simultaneously allowed by the prediction and potentially treated as falsifying.
